purpose: A server that will not start is the most common single outcome in this cohort, and 'connect_failed' on its own is useless to a buyer. These patterns classify WHY, against the stderr captured at launch and the error returned by the server/discover probe. Classification is diagnostic only: it does not feed any score, which is why it lives outside the scoring rubric and outside the config hash.

attribution_legend.server: A property of the server. It genuinely will not run in this condition.
attribution_legend.harness: Caused by a deliberate choice of this harness. Must not be reported as a defect of the server.
attribution_legend.environment: Caused by the host or the network at run time. Not attributable to either side.

classes.label: Refuses to start without valid credentials
classes.buyer_note: Cannot be inspected, evaluated, or audited by anyone who does not already hold live credentials for it, including a prospective buyer.

classes.label: Requires instance-specific deployment details before it will list tools
patterns: host or apiBasePath must be provided
Set these in your MCP configuration
classes.buyer_note: Needs a host, account, or base path filled in before it will even enumerate its tools. Nobody can evaluate it cold, and the registry entry does not carry the values it demands.

classes.label: Requires an environment variable the registry entry does not document a default for
patterns: must be included in custom levels
classes.buyer_note: The registry entry is incomplete: it declares the variable but not the value the server will accept. A first-run failure for anyone following the listing.

classes.label: Ships a binary fetched by a postinstall script, which this harness suppresses
patterns: Could not locate the bindings file
classes.buyer_note: Not a defect the buyer would hit with a normal install. It is a supply-chain note: the package downloads an executable at install time, so its contents are not fixed by the version number alone.

classes.label: Reaches the network before it will serve tools
classes.buyer_note: Startup depends on a third-party service being reachable and willing. Tool availability is not a property of the installed package.

classes.label: Blocks startup on indexing its working directory
classes.buyer_note: Runs analysis before it will answer tools/list, so time-to-first-tool depends on the size of whatever directory it is launched in. In an empty directory it still failed to complete the handshake inside 45 seconds.

classes.label: Closed the connection with no diagnostic output at all
classes.match_when: stderr is empty and the transport closed
classes.buyer_note: The worst failure mode to debug: nothing on stderr, nothing on the protocol. An operator has no thread to pull.

classes.label: Answers neither handshake
classes.match_when: The server/discover probe returned no modern verdict AND the initialize handshake was answered with a JSON-RPC method-not-found error (-32601). The initialize answer is the evidence: it proves the process was alive and speaking JSON-RPC while implementing neither handshake method. The pin-mode discover probe cannot supply that distinction on its own, since it reports a 2025 server and a JSON-RPC refusal with the same error. Any other failure of initialize is left to the stderr patterns.
classes.buyer_note: Unreachable by any conforming client of either era. The 2026-07-28 specification makes server/discover mandatory for servers, so a process that answers it with a protocol error and also fails initialize is not merely old: it is unusable by a current client and by a legacy one alike.

changelog: 1.1.0 (2026-08-13): added no_handshake_response, for a server that answers neither the 2026-07-28 server/discover exchange nor the 2025 initialize handshake. Introduced with the dual-era probe in harness 0.1.4: before it, a server that had migrated to the stateless core would have been recorded as a server-side connect failure, which is the one misattribution the split exists to prevent.
1.0.2 (2026-08-11): added requires_deployment_config after three servers in the verification pair failed on missing host/email/base-path rather than on credentials as such.

1.0.1 (2026-08-11): scans_working_directory re-attributed from harness to server. Harness 0.1.1 launches every server inside its own empty sandbox directory, so a server that still blocks startup on indexing is doing analysis eagerly that should be lazy — that is its own behaviour, not an artifact of where it was started.
1.0.0 (2026-08-11): initial classes, derived from the first full sweep.
